doc.title: Kenny Barron — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Philadelphia roots and arrival in New York
title: Deciding on music and meeting his Philadelphia peers
summary: Having met players his own age such as Sonny Fortune and Reggie Workman, he decides on music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Then, from there – you’re in high school. So you’re already determined? You want – this is what you want to do, make a career in music?

Yeah, the die was cast. I was definitely deciding, I want to play music. Plus I had met – by that time I had met my peers, so to speak, guys who were my age, because when I was working with Mel Melvin, they were all much older. They were in their 40s. Then I was like, 14. I had met the guys who were playing from my generation around Philly. So I was starting to work quite a bit. Sonny Fortune was among those. He was a couple of years older, but he was around. We were playing. And a saxophone player named Jimmy Bass. Quite a few others. I started playing a lot. Reggie Workman, who’s also a few years older. He was back and forth between New York and Philly. That was a great time.
